# BrickBreaker — Agent Notes

## One-liner
2D brick-breaker arcade game in C# / Unity 6 (6000.3.5f1), where all GameObjects (walls, paddle, ball, bricks, HUD) are created programmatically at runtime — no prefabs, no manual scene wiring.

## Run it
```
# Open in Unity 6 (6000.3.5f1), then open Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity and press Play.
# There is no CLI/dotnet build path — Assembly-CSharp.csproj is generated by Unity for IDE use only.
# Headless build (untested in this repo):
#   "C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.3.5f1\Editor\Unity.exe" -projectPath . -quit -batchmode -buildTarget StandaloneWindows64
```

## Gotchas
- Bootstrap is implicit: `BrickBreakerGame.Bootstrap()` uses `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(AfterSceneLoad)]` to spawn the controller. The SampleScene is intentionally near-empty — do not "fix" it by adding a manager GameObject.
- Sprites are built from `Texture2D.whiteTexture` at runtime; there are no art assets to import. PPU defaults can make things look tiny — adjust `Camera.orthographicSize` rather than hunting for missing sprites.
- Input uses the new Input System (`UnityEngine.InputSystem`, `Keyboard.current`, `Mouse.current`). If input silently breaks, check Project Settings -> Player -> Active Input Handling is set to "Input System Package" (or Both).
- HUD uses legacy `UnityEngine.UI.Text` with font `LegacyRuntime.ttf`, not TextMeshPro.
- Rigidbody2D uses Unity 6's `bodyType` API; do not regress to the deprecated `isKinematic` setter.
- `Library/`, `Logs/`, `Temp/`, `UserSettings/` are present locally but gitignored — never stage them.

## Non-obvious conventions
- All four scripts live flat in `Assets/Scripts/` with no namespace. `BrickBreakerGame` is the orchestrator; `PaddleController` / `BallController` / `Brick` are thin and call back into it via `OnBrickDestroyed` / `OnBallLost`.
- Public fields on `BrickBreakerGame` (columns, rows, ballSpeed, etc.) are the tuning surface — tweak there, not in scattered constants.
- Bricks are colored via an HSV gradient computed in `CreateBricks()`, not from a palette asset.

See README.md for project description, tech stack, feature list, and full control reference.
